name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Integrate a capability into the product task

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the product benefit and capability prerequisites before entering the technology-specific procedure. Avoid adding a system integration solely to decorate an existing flow.
2. Define consent/account/capability availability and the meaningful result, cancel, failure and recovery paths applicable to that integration. Keep sensitive information and system ownership clear.
3. Preserve supplied branding, hardware and platform qualifications. HIG states experience expectations; verify current APIs against implementation documentation when writing framework-specific code.
4. Deliver an integration contract or correction in the existing stack, with source-supported choices, fallbacks and evidence limits. Do not claim a payment, health, spatial or connected-device runtime test from a static specimen.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make

name: apple-hig-live-photos
description: Use when designing or reviewing Live Photo editing, playback identity, whole-asset preview/sharing, download readiness, or still-image fallback.
---

# Preserve the captured moment as one asset

Read [Live Photos](../../references/live-photos.md). Inspect asset support, edits, download state, preview/sharing, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing photo pipeline. The source excludes watchOS; visionOS viewing is supported but capture is not. Do not promise Live Photo behavior where only still-image support exists.

Treat still, surrounding frames, and sound as one captured moment. If an edit can apply consistently to every frame, preserve the live asset; otherwise offer an explicit conversion to a still instead of silently editing only its poster frame. Do not split audio and frames into separate presentations that change the asset's identity.

Expose whole-asset preview before sharing and always provide ordinary-photo sharing. Define download progress and readiness so a live affordance is not shown as available before the data is usable. Use a subtle motion hint or a system badge when movement cannot demonstrate the content. Avoid a video-style play button; keep badges consistently placed without obscuring the image. Unsupported destinations should receive/show a still rather than a homemade approximation of Live Photo playback.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a filter changes only the thumbnail, sharing immediately sends motion the person has not previewed, and a large video Play triangle covers the image. Decision: edits and sharing must represent the complete captured moment. After, the filter applies across frames or offers clear still conversion, preview includes the whole live asset, and a subtle appropriate indicator distinguishes it while ordinary-photo sharing remains available.

Deliver an edit/readiness/preview/share state contract and corrected artifact or implementation. Fail if poster and motion edits disagree, sharing exposes unpreviewed content without a preview route, or an unsupported environment implies live playback. Actual asset preservation, sound/frame synchronization, export, and device playback need supported tests; static UI evidence proves only the designed states.

Use [Photo editing](../apple-hig-photo-editing/SKILL.md) for extension cancel/save behavior and [Images](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-images/SKILL.md) for format/density work.

# Live Photos Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Live Photos combines a still with sound and frames captured before/after the shutter. Pressing a Live Photo plays that captured moment. Preserve its consistent interactive identity. ## Best practices Apply edits to every frame or offer conversion to a still. Do not split the audio/frames into separate presentations. Let people preview the entire live asset before sharing and always offer ordinary-photo sharing. Show download progress and readiness. In unsupported environments, display a still rather than recreating playback. Distinguish live assets with a subtle custom motion hint, or a system badge when movement is impossible; avoid a video-style play button. Keep badges consistently positioned, usually in a corner. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS rules; watchOS is unsupported. ### visionOS Live Photos can be viewed but not captured. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

name: apple-hig-activity-views
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting system sharing, custom activities, and share or action extensions.
---

# Share the current content through its context

Read [the activity-view guide](../../references/activity-views.md). The procedure is application advice; distinguish activity views from Mac share/action extensions.

Inspect the content types, selection, Share entry point, target platform, and create/review/adapt request. Determine whether a proposed extension transfers information elsewhere or acts on it in context. Record available content and current task eligibility; do not assume every system destination supports every payload.

Use the standard Share button and system presentation where supported. Offer only relevant custom activities, avoid duplicate system actions, and name specialized variants distinctly with concise verbs. Do not prescribe system task order, which the app cannot control. Choose a familiar composition view; if custom UI is necessary keep it short and related to the host app. An extension is already modal, so avoid another modal except a necessary alert.

Implement the share payload/activities, deliver a payload-to-destination/action specification, or review exact relevance and handoff failures. If work continues after dismissal, specify background continuation and status in the main app; notify for problems rather than routine completion. On Mac use supported share/action extension entry points without claiming a Mac activity-view component; tvOS/watchOS lack activity views.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a document share sheet adds branded `Acme Print`, duplicates Print, and closes only after a large upload finishes. Decision: the custom action is redundant and long work should not trap the extension. After: retain system Print, name the distinct transfer `Send for Approval`, dismiss after accepting the task, and surface its status/problem in the app.

Deliver the artifact plus payload, custom eligibility, dismissal, and continuation contract. Verify with the actual selected content, unavailable destinations, cancellation, and post-dismissal work. Fail for missing payload, duplicate misleading actions, nested modal traps, or claimed ordering control. Separate extension execution from inspected specification.

Load [collaboration-and-sharing](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-collaboration-and-sharing/SKILL.md) for permissions or [modality](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-modality/SKILL.md) for extension exits.

# Activity views Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-views) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. The system share sheet offers contextual sharing, common actions, and frequently used apps. It appears as a sheet or popover according to device and orientation. App-specific activities normally precede general system actions; people can customize the action list. Extensions can expose share/action functionality in other apps, including on macOS even though Mac has no activity-view component. ## Best practices Use the standard Share button to reveal it. Exclude irrelevant tasks and show only currently appropriate custom tasks; system task order is not app-controlled. Avoid duplicating existing actions such as Print. Give a specialized variation a clearly distinct name. Use a short verb phrase for custom actions without product/company branding; share destinations can use the company name beneath their icon. Prefer SF Symbols; center a custom glyph in an approximately 70×70-pixel area. ## Share and action extensions Share extensions transfer contextual information to another app or service; action extensions operate on content without leaving context. iOS/iPadOS expose both through the share sheet. On Mac, sharing comes from toolbar or context-menu Share; actions may come from embedded-content controls, a toolbar, or Finder quick actions. Prefer the familiar system composition view for sharing. Include the app name for an action extension and use related app interface elements when a custom UI is necessary. Keep the task to few steps. Avoid stacking another modal over the already modal extension, except a necessary alert. Share extensions inherit the app icon; actions should use a meaningful symbol or glyph. Continue long work in the background after dismissal and show status in the main app. Notify only about a problem rather than routine completion. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, or visionOS rules are specified. Activity views themselves are unsupported in macOS, tvOS, and watchOS; Mac share/action extensions remain supported as described above. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Sheets](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sheets) [Popovers](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers) #### Developer documentation — UIKit — UIKit — Foundation #### Videos

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.
---

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. item.text: The brief identifies three connected failures: import loses the Live Photo, the grid autoplays every motion asset, and export drops the still. The revised contract will preserve each captured moment as one asset, make playback deliberate, and offer an explicit still-photo export for unsupported recipients.

# Revised interaction specification: iPhone family album

This replaces the behavior described in "'`interface.md`. It is a framework-agnostic design contract, not an implementation or an assertion that an Apple SDK is available.

## Decisions and source support

1. **Preserve the captured moment on import.** Store the still, surrounding frames, sound (when present), and their association as one logical album item. Generate thumbnails separately; never replace the source with a thumbnail or flatten it silently. If complete import cannot be supported, retain the source pending recovery and offer “Retry import”, “Import Still Photo”, or “Cancel”. Explain that importing a still omits motion and sound. Existing flattened imports cannot be reconstructed without their originals; offer reimport when available. Whole-asset identity and explicit still conversion follow [Live Photos — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos#Best-practices). Retaining originals and these recovery labels are product decisions.
2. **Use a quiet grid.** Show still thumbnails; no automatic playback or sound, including during rapid scrolling. Mark known Live Photos with a consistently placed, unobtrusive corner badge and text identity “LIVE”; keep essential image content visible. A badge identifies the asset type, not download readiness. Avoid a video-style play triangle. This applies the badge guidance in [Live Photos](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos#Best-practices); disabling all grid autoplay is this product’s decision.
3. **Provide deliberate whole-asset preview.** Open detail on thumbnail activation. Show the still initially. Press-and-hold the image to play the captured moment; release stops and returns to the still. Also provide a labeled “Preview Live Photo” action, which plays once and becomes “Stop Preview”. Include synchronized sound when present, subject to the user’s audio setting; show “Sound On”/“Sound Off” and allow adjustment. Do not present sound or frames as separately browsable media. Preview remains available before export, including all before/after frames and sound. It is offered, not compulsory. See [Live Photos](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos#Best-practices).
4. **Make export format explicit.** Offer “Live Photo — Still, motion, and sound” and “Still Photo — No motion or sound” before handoff. Ordinary-photo export is always a route; it may require downloading the still. A supported live export includes the associated still and motion/sound, never motion alone. Unsupported destinations receive a still. Unknown support must not be treated as verified live support. See [Live Photos](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-photos#Best-practices).
5. **Use platform sharing when available.** A standard Share entry point opens the export preparation flow, then hands the chosen representation to the system share presentation when the host supports it. Do not imitate a system sheet or assume its ordering is controllable. Without such integration, use a clearly labeled app export destination flow with the same payload rules. No duplicate custom Print/Save activities. This follows [Activity views — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-views#Best-practices); the short format-preparation step is a product decision.

## Asset and readiness contract

```text
AlbumItem = {
  id, revision, kind: still | live,
  sourceStill, sourceMotionWithSound?, association?,
  stillState: absent | fetching | ready | failed,
  liveState: absent | fetching | validating | ready | failed,
  originalRetained, conversionExplicit
}
liveReady = stillState == ready AND liveState == ready
            AND associationVerified AND completeMomentValidated
```

`ready` requires readable, associated components, not merely a known file name. No SDK-specific encoding or association format is prescribed. The implementation must supply a validated live import/export adapter; without one, report live capability unavailable and offer explicit still conversion. Do not manufacture Live Photo playback from unrelated video files.

| State | Visible contract | Available actions and transition |
|---|---|---|
| Still ready, live remote | Still plus LIVE identity; “Download to preview motion and sound” | “Download Live Photo” starts fetch; still export remains available |
| Downloading | “Downloading Live Photo” plus measured progress if known; otherwise indeterminate status | “Cancel Download”; preserve still and any source originals |
| Validating | “Preparing Live Photo” | Cancel preparation; preview/live export unavailable |
| Fully ready | Still plus LIVE identity | Hold or Preview action; both export formats available |
| Download/validation failure | Still plus “Live Photo unavailable” and readable reason | “Retry”; still export; no enabled live playback affordance |
| Still unavailable | Placeholder identifying the item and its state | Fetch/retry still; do not export a nonexistent still |
| Permanently missing live data | “Only the still photo is available” | Still export; offer reimport if original can be supplied |

Canceling or failing a fetch does not change the asset’s type or convert it. Do not label a known Live Photo as an ordinary photo just because its motion is remote. Preview stops on navigation, scrolling away, interruption, or backgrounding; it does not resume automatically. Starting a new preview stops the old one. Playback completion returns to the still. No queued autoplay after a download completes.

If editing is later offered, apply edits consistently to the still and all frames, or explicitly offer “Save as Still Photo” while retaining the original. Poster-only edits must never masquerade as a consistently edited live asset.

## Export interaction and payload contract

Scope: the currently opened item. Batch export is outside this revision. Format selection is local to this export; default to Live Photo only when complete live export is available. Otherwise show why it is unavailable and offer Still Photo without silently selecting a lossy operation.

1. Activate Share. Show the selected item, format choices, whole-asset preview route, and a concise payload description. “Preview Live Photo” includes sound when enabled; disclose if sound is off. “Continue” prepares the selected format; “Cancel” returns to the item unchanged.
2. If chosen data is remote, expose download/preparation status and cancel/retry. Readiness gates handoff. A live failure offers “Retry” or an explicit “Use Still Photo”; never silently substitutes.
3. Resolve destination capability conservatively:

| Destination evidence | Export result |
|---|---|
| Verified complete Live Photo support | In Live Photo mode, hand off one associated logical asset containing still + motion + sound when present |
| Known still-only | Show “This destination supports still photos only. Motion and sound won’t be included.” Offer “Send Still Photo” or “Cancel” |
| Unknown or unverified | Show “Live Photo support can’t be verified.” Offer still export or return to choose a verified destination; do not promise live delivery |
| Any destination in Still Photo mode | Send only the still; retain the original album asset |

If destination capability cannot be inspected inside a system sharing integration, constrain that handoff to the explicitly chosen still format; expose live export only through a verified route. Do not claim the system sheet can supply capabilities it does not expose. Do not silently fall back after the user selected Live Photo.

4. Before dispatch, snapshot the item ID/revision and representation. If the item changes during preparation, discard the stale prepared copy and ask the person to review the updated item. Never combine components from different revisions.
5. Cancel before dispatch deletes temporary output and returns with the item and format choice intact. Preparation/dispatch failure retains the original and offers retry. Prevent duplicate dispatch while a request is pending. Dismiss system sharing through its supported lifecycle; show any app-owned continuing transfer status in the album, with cancel only where supported. Report “Handed to [destination]” when that is all the adapter can establish. Say “Sent” only with an actual completion result; do not claim recipient playback or receipt without evidence. Problems remain actionable in the album. See [Activity views — Share and action extensions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-views#Share-and-action-extensions).

```text
prepare(item, chosenFormat):
  snapshot = freeze(item.id, item.revision)
  require chosenFormat == still ? stillReady : liveReady
  payload = chosenFormat == still
      ? exportStill(snapshot)
      : exportAssociatedWholeMoment(snapshot)
  validate(payload, snapshot, chosenFormat)
  return payload   // no dispatch yet

handoff(payload, destination):
  if payload.isLive AND destination.support != verifiedLive:
    return explicitStillChoiceOrCancel
  dispatchOnce(payload, destination)
  recordOnlyObservedOutcome()
```

## Motion and accessible operation

These are specified requirements awaiting execution. Grid identity, readiness, errors, and export consequences use text or semantics as well as badges; no meaning relies solely on animation or sound. Use iOS default 44 × 44 pt activation areas for app-owned actions, with sufficient separation. Allow text enlargement to at least 200% without losing the format consequences, status, or cancel/retry controls. Label the image with its supplied family caption or neutral identity, asset type, and readiness; label actions by outcome. Do not invent descriptions of family members or audible content.

Press-and-hold is optional: assistive activation of Preview starts one complete preview and Stop ends it. All export decisions remain reachable without timed gestures. Reduce Motion uses a static badge and instant or restrained fades for interface transitions; explicit media preview remains optional and stoppable, never needed to identify the asset or choose an export. Honor applicable flashing-content accommodations when supported; expose any capability limit rather than claim compliance. Family captions/transcripts may describe meaningful sound or visual events when supplied; this design does not claim automatic media description or transcription.

Support and later verify the full task with assistive input, including VoiceOver, Switch Control, and Full Keyboard Access. Sources: [Accessibility — Vision, Mobility, Cognitive](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) and [Motion — Best practices / Providing feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion). Removing grid autoplay and the precise control/state contract are product decisions, not quoted universal Apple rules.

## Worked before/after

Example fixture: “Grandma’s birthday” consists of still S, surrounding frames M, and birthday wishes A, associated as L. Aunt May’s destination accepts only still photos.

**Before, as reported in the brief:** Import flattens L without notice. Motion assets autoplay throughout a fast grid. Export drops the still without warning. The brief does not establish exactly which remaining files reach Aunt May or how her client renders them.

**After, specified:** Import retains S+M+A as L and shows one still thumbnail with LIVE identity. Scrolling causes no playback. Open L: if M+A are remote, download them with visible status; no preview is offered as ready until validation succeeds. Activate Preview to see all frames with synchronized birthday wishes, then stop or let it finish. Share describes the complete live payload and offers Still Photo. On selecting May’s known still-only destination, disclose the loss of motion and sound. “Send Still Photo” sends S alone; Cancel sends nothing. L remains S+M+A in the album for a later verified live destination. A failed download still permits S export when S is ready, with the same explicit choice.

## Acceptance checks and audit status

The following are implementation acceptance scenarios, not executed tests:

| Check | Required observation |
|---|---|
| Complete import and round trip | A known fixture retains associated still, all frames, sound when present, and timing through import and live export; decode and compare content/association, not file extensions alone |
| Import failure / existing flattening | No silent conversion; explicit still choice or retry/cancel; old flattened items do not acquire fabricated motion |
| Fast grid traversal | No cell starts motion/audio; badges stay consistently placed; rapid navigation never queues playback |
| Remote asset | Badge identifies type while readiness says download; preview/live handoff cannot run early; determinate progress is factual |
| Interrupted or failed fetch | Cancel/retry works; original and still survive; completion does not autoplay |
| Whole preview | Before/after frames and sound remain synchronized; hold/release and accessible Preview/Stop work; leaving stops playback |
| Live export | Verified destination receives still plus associated motion/sound; no component from another revision; export leaves source intact |
| Still / unsupported / unknown | Still choice produces an ordinary still; unsupported and unknown routes disclose limitations; no motion-only output or homemade live simulation |
| Cancel / error / pending dispatch | No dispatch on pre-handoff cancel; retry is possible; repeated activation cannot duplicate a pending dispatch; outcome text matches actual evidence |
| Preferences and assistive input | Reduce Motion retains identity/status; 200% text retains actions/consequences; actions have usable activation areas and can be reached/activated with assistive input |
| Future editing guard | Either every frame and still agree, or conversion to still is explicit |

**Passed — static specification review:** `interface.md` was read. This document supplies decisions addressing all three reported defects and the still-only recipient case, plus readiness, preview, payload, cancellation, and recovery contracts. Installed root, selected families, topic procedures, and source guides were read in order, one file per command. The topic index was searched for Live Photos and sharing/accessibility concepts.

**Failed — supplied design against this contract:** The brief explicitly reports silent flattening, indiscriminate grid autoplay, and still-dropping export. These are reported design failures, not independently reproduced runtime findings.

**Not executed:** Every runtime acceptance scenario above; real asset import/export/decoding, recipient compatibility, synchronization, download progress, system share integration, device playback, geometry/contrast measurement, assistive-technology operation, SDK compilation, GUI execution, and physical comfort testing.

## Evidence limits

Inputs were the short local `interface.md` and installed apple-hig guidance only. No source code, sample assets, screenshots, destination capability records, or running app were supplied. The installed guides are derivative snapshots dated 2026-10-25, not SDK documentation or independently verified current Apple behavior. Official links above identify source articles; they were not opened. No web, device, Apple SDK, GUI, or accessibility execution occurred. There is no evidence of source conflicts in the consulted passages; absence of a platform subsection is not proof of capability. Concrete formats, metadata preservation, transport support, recipient behavior, and framework feasibility require implementation evidence before shipping. This specification preserves the existing unknown framework and requires adapters rather than assuming Apple APIs exist.
EOF'

Preview stops on navigation, scrolling away, interruption, or backgrounding; it does not resume automatically. Starting a new preview stops the old one. Playback completion returns to the still. No queued autoplay after a download completes.

If editing is later offered, apply edits consistently to the still and all frames, or explicitly offer “Save as Still Photo” while retaining the original. Poster-only edits must never masquerade as a consistently edited live asset.

## Export interaction and payload contract

Scope: the currently opened item. Batch export is outside this revision. Format selection is local to this export; default to Live Photo only when complete live export is available. Otherwise show why it is unavailable and offer Still Photo without silently selecting a lossy operation.

1. Activate Share. Show the selected item, format choices, whole-asset preview route, and a concise payload description. “Preview Live Photo” includes sound when enabled; disclose if sound is off. “Continue” prepares the selected format; “Cancel” returns to the item unchanged.
2. If chosen data is remote, expose download/preparation status and cancel/retry. Readiness gates handoff. A live failure offers “Retry” or an explicit “Use Still Photo”; never silently substitutes.
3. Resolve destination capability conservatively:

| Destination evidence | Export result |
|---|---|
| Verified complete Live Photo support | In Live Photo mode, hand off one associated logical asset containing still + motion + sound when present |
| Known still-only | Show “This destination supports still photos only. Motion and sound won’t be included.” Offer “Send Still Photo” or “Cancel” |
| Unknown or unverified | Show “Live Photo support can’t be verified.” Offer still export or return to choose a verified destination; do not promise live delivery |
| Any destination in Still Photo mode | Send only the still; retain the original album asset |

If destination capability cannot be inspected inside a system sharing integration, constrain that handoff to the explicitly chosen still format; expose live export only through a verified route. Do not claim the system sheet can supply capabilities it does not expose. Do not silently fall back after the user selected Live Photo.

4. Before dispatch, snapshot the item ID/revision and representation. If the item changes during preparation, discard the stale prepared copy and ask the person to review the updated item. Never combine components from different revisions.
5. Cancel before dispatch deletes temporary output and returns with the item and format choice intact. Preparation/dispatch failure retains the original and offers retry. Prevent duplicate dispatch while a request is pending. Dismiss system sharing through its supported lifecycle; show any app-owned continuing transfer status in the album, with cancel only where supported. Report “Handed to [destination]” when that is all the adapter can establish. Say “Sent” only with an actual completion result; do not claim recipient playback or receipt without evidence. Problems remain actionable in the album. See [Activity views — Share and action extensions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/activity-views#Share-and-action-extensions).

```text
prepare(item, chosenFormat):
  snapshot = freeze(item.id, item.revision)
  require chosenFormat == still ? stillReady : liveReady
  payload = chosenFormat == still
      ? exportStill(snapshot)
      : exportAssociatedWholeMoment(snapshot)
  validate(payload, snapshot, chosenFormat)
  return payload   // no dispatch yet

handoff(payload, destination):
  if payload.isLive AND destination.support != verifiedLive:
    return explicitStillChoiceOrCancel
  dispatchOnce(payload, destination)
  recordOnlyObservedOutcome()
```

## Motion and accessible operation

These are specified requirements awaiting execution. Grid identity, readiness, errors, and export consequences use text or semantics as well as badges; no meaning relies solely on animation or sound. Use iOS default 44 × 44 pt activation areas for app-owned actions, with sufficient separation. Allow text enlargement to at least 200% without losing the format consequences, status, or cancel/retry controls. Label the image with its supplied family caption or neutral identity, asset type, and readiness; label actions by outcome. Do not invent descriptions of family members or audible content.

Press-and-hold is optional: assistive activation of Preview starts one complete preview and Stop ends it. All export decisions remain reachable without timed gestures. Reduce Motion uses a static badge and instant or restrained fades for interface transitions; explicit media preview remains optional and stoppable, never needed to identify the asset or choose an export. Honor applicable flashing-content accommodations when supported; expose any capability limit rather than claim compliance. Family captions/transcripts may describe meaningful sound or visual events when supplied; this design does not claim automatic media description or transcription.

Support and later verify the full task with assistive input, including VoiceOver, Switch Control, and Full Keyboard Access. Sources: [Accessibility — Vision, Mobility, Cognitive](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) and [Motion — Best practices / Providing feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion). Removing grid autoplay and the precise control/state contract are product decisions, not quoted universal Apple rules.

## Worked before/after

Example fixture: “Grandma’s birthday” consists of still S, surrounding frames M, and birthday wishes A, associated as L. Aunt May’s destination accepts only still photos.

**Before, as reported in the brief:** Import flattens L without notice. Motion assets autoplay throughout a fast grid. Export drops the still without warning. The brief does not establish exactly which remaining files reach Aunt May or how her client renders them.

**After, specified:** Import retains S+M+A as L and shows one still thumbnail with LIVE identity. Scrolling causes no playback. Open L: if M+A are remote, download them with visible status; no preview is offered as ready until validation succeeds. Activate Preview to see all frames with synchronized birthday wishes, then stop or let it finish. Share describes the complete live payload and offers Still Photo. On selecting May’s known still-only destination, disclose the loss of motion and sound. “Send Still Photo” sends S alone; Cancel sends nothing. L remains S+M+A in the album for a later verified live destination. A failed download still permits S export when S is ready, with the same explicit choice.

## Acceptance checks and audit status

The following are implementation acceptance scenarios, not executed tests:

| Check | Required observation |
|---|---|
| Complete import and round trip | A known fixture retains associated still, all frames, sound when present, and timing through import and live export; decode and compare content/association, not file extensions alone |
| Import failure / existing flattening | No silent conversion; explicit still choice or retry/cancel; old flattened items do not acquire fabricated motion |
| Fast grid traversal | No cell starts motion/audio; badges stay consistently placed; rapid navigation never queues playback |
| Remote asset | Badge identifies type while readiness says download; preview/live handoff cannot run early; determinate progress is factual |
| Interrupted or failed fetch | Cancel/retry works; original and still survive; completion does not autoplay |
| Whole preview | Before/after frames and sound remain synchronized; hold/release and accessible Preview/Stop work; leaving stops playback |
| Live export | Verified destination receives still plus associated motion/sound; no component from another revision; export leaves source intact |
| Still / unsupported / unknown | Still choice produces an ordinary still; unsupported and unknown routes disclose limitations; no motion-only output or homemade live simulation |
| Cancel / error / pending dispatch | No dispatch on pre-handoff cancel; retry is possible; repeated activation cannot duplicate a pending dispatch; outcome text matches actual evidence |
| Preferences and assistive input | Reduce Motion retains identity/status; 200% text retains actions/consequences; actions have usable activation areas and can be reached/activated with assistive input |
| Future editing guard | Either every frame and still agree, or conversion to still is explicit |

**Passed — static specification review:** `interface.md` was read. This document supplies decisions addressing all three reported defects and the still-only recipient case, plus readiness, preview, payload, cancellation, and recovery contracts. Installed root, selected families, topic procedures, and source guides were read in order, one file per command. The topic index was searched for Live Photos and sharing/accessibility concepts.

**Failed — supplied design against this contract:** The brief explicitly reports silent flattening, indiscriminate grid autoplay, and still-dropping export. These are reported design failures, not independently reproduced runtime findings.

**Not executed:** Every runtime acceptance scenario above; real asset import/export/decoding, recipient compatibility, synchronization, download progress, system share integration, device playback, geometry/contrast measurement, assistive-technology operation, SDK compilation, GUI execution, and physical comfort testing.

## Evidence limits

Inputs were the short local `interface.md` and installed apple-hig guidance only. No source code, sample assets, screenshots, destination capability records, or running app were supplied. The installed guides are derivative snapshots dated 2026-10-25, not SDK documentation or independently verified current Apple behavior. Official links above identify source articles; they were not opened. No web, device, Apple SDK, GUI, or accessibility execution occurred. There is no evidence of source conflicts in the consulted passages; absence of a platform subsection is not proof of capability. Concrete formats, metadata preservation, transport support, recipient behavior, and framework feasibility require implementation evidence before shipping. This specification preserves the existing unknown framework and requires adapters rather than assuming Apple APIs exist.
